messages:
incident-bot: :pager: SEV2 - routing anomalies detected: multiple region fallback loops observed between us-east <-> us-west with secondary bounce to eu. Auto-fallback triggered 24 times in 8m. Investigate.

Priya S: acked, paging oncall. I’m on it.

incident-bot: Pager -> @Priya S, @Alex T oncall.

Alex T: looking at routing logs now, noticing rapid health flips from 10.0.4.12 (us-east) to 10.1.7.9 (us-west). TTL for fallback is 30s, but health marks flip faster.

Sam R: grabbing probe logs from probe-agent in us-east. suspecting transient probe failure making the smart-router mark instances unhealthy immediately.

Priya S: are probes returning 5xx or connection resets?

Sam R: snippets: 
```
[us-east] 2026-03-15T10:12:03Z PROBE health ok
[us-east] 2026-03-15T10:12:04Z PROBE connection reset
[us-east] 2026-03-15T10:12:05Z PROBE fail count 1/1 -> UNHEALTHY
[us-west] 2026-03-15T10:12:06Z PROBE observed traffic spike, marking healthy
[eu] 2026-03-15T10:12:07Z PROBE start fallback
```
Looks like consecutive_failures for the health check is set to 1 on the smart-router policy.

Jen L: that would explain ping-pong. policy immediately evicts a node on any transient failure -> routes to next region -> that region sees extra load -> transient errors -> routes back.

Alex T: confirmed, routing policy config: `fallback.health_consecutive_failures: 1` and `fallback.hysteresis_ms: 0`. Oops. Who changed this?

Priya S: change history shows a config push by infra-deploy last night to enable faster failover for a different service. Looks like a blanket policy.

Sam R: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable cross-region fallback for affected customer pool, 2) increase consecutive_failures to 3 and add hysteresis 15000ms, 3) restart probe-agent on us-east to clear bad state.

Priya S: I’ll execute 1 and 2. Alex, can you do the rollout of policy? Sam, take probe restarts.

Alex T: running: `redwoodctl routing update --scope dedicated:us-east --set fallback.health_consecutive_failures=3 --set fallback.hysteresis_ms=15000`

ops-bot: action-log: routing policy updated by Alex T (change-id c73b2f).

Sam R: restarting probe agent in us-east: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/probe-agent -l region=us-east`

Priya S: pulled the cross-region fallback toggle for the impacted dedicated pool: `redwoodctl routing toggle-cross-region --pool d-495 --state off --reason "incident mitigation"`

Alex T: policy pushed, verifying. Running a small canary traffic test to ensure no client disruption.

Sam R: probe restarts finished. initial steady state, probe logs show fewer resets.

Priya S: monitoring metrics: fallback count dropped from 24->2 in last 10min. error rate on impacted targets down from 5.3% -> 0.8%. tail latency spikes reduced.

Jen L: customer impact: 3 enterprise customers on dedicated us-east saw increased errors and elevated latency for ~12m during peak. No data loss, just transient 5xx and timeouts. Customer success notified for the three accounts.

Priya S: paging follow-up: escalate to infra change review to prevent blanket policy pushes. Need a guard on `consecutive_failures` global overrides.

Alex T: I'll open a CL to the routing policy defaults and add an approval gate for global changes. Also add an automated canary that prevents rollout if fallback health thresholds are lowered below 2.

Sam R: Suggestion: add a short cooldown window before marking region unhealthy when cross-region load > threshold. Will draft RFC.

Jen L: handoff to Jen for postmortem and customer comms. Priya, Alex — please attach logs and config diffs to the postmortem ticket.

Priya S: attaching important artifacts: `s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/1987654321/probe-logs.tar.gz`, routing policy diff: `-- fallback.health_consecutive_failures: 1 -> 3`, `-- fallback.hysteresis_ms: 0 -> 15000`.

incident-bot: Incident SEV2 resolved. duration 0h 12m. Auto-close in 30m unless `reopen` requested.

Jen L: closing loop: postmortem owner assigned -> Jen L. Timeline & action items will be posted to #postmortems this afternoon.

Priya S: thanks everyone. leaving short-term mitigation (no cross-region fallback) in place for 1h to stabilize; will revert once we confirm stability and can deploy safer policy change permanently. :thumbsup:
